issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states an 'if and only if' characterization of kappa-optimality (x_1•x_1 = x_n•x_n) without any multiplicity hypothesis and explicitly asserts that in the nonsmooth case one may simply pick x_1, x_n in the respective eigenspaces. The proof, however, only differentiates via Lemma lem:optkappacond, which requires singleton eigenvalues, and concludes from ∇κ(e)=0. When λ_max or λ_min is repeated, optimality of d=e is 0 ∈ ∂(λ_max − κ λ_min)(e), i.e. existence of PSD trace-one W_1, W_n supported on the two eigenspaces with diag(W_1)=diag(W_n); this is a convex-hull condition and is strictly weaker than the existence of a single eigenvector pair. Concrete counterexample to the 'only if' direction: A = 2I − ee^T/3 in R^3 has λ_max = 2 with eigenspace e^⊥ and λ_min = 1 with eigenvector w = e/√3. By permutation symmetry and quasiconvexity, d = e is κ-optimal (indeed W_1 = (I − ww^T)/2 gives diag(W_1) = e/3 = w•w). But a unit x_1 ∈ e^⊥ with x_1•x_1 = e/3 would need x_1 = (±1,±1,±1)/√3, none of which is orthogonal to e. Hence no eigenvector pair satisfies (eq:optkappascaled) although A is κ-optimally diagonally preconditioned.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that λ_max(AD) and λ_min(AD) are simple to the 'if and only if' statement, and either delete the nonsmooth sentence or replace it by the correct subdifferential condition: d=e is optimal iff there exist PSD, trace-one matrices W_1, W_n supported on the max/min eigenspaces with diag(W_1) = diag(W_n) (sufficiency of a single pair remains true).
issues.overall_effect: The stated necessary-and-sufficient characterization of κ-optimal diagonal preconditioning holds only under the (unstated) hypothesis that λ_max and λ_min are simple; the advertised nonsmooth extension is false in the necessity direction. Downstream uses (Prop. prop:nonuniqd, Lemma lem:optAforkappaconstr, the construction in Section 3.3) assume singleton eigenvalues and remain valid.
issues.title: Optimality characterization in Theorem thm:optcondkappa is only proved (and only true) for singleton extreme eigenvalues; the claimed extension to the nonsmooth case fails
issues.why_classification: The smooth-case result survives unchanged and dependents are unaffected, but the stated scope (general, including nonsmooth) must be withdrawn or replaced by a genuinely different convex-hull characterization requiring a new (if standard) subdifferential argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Second, since \Cref{GD} is a subgradient method, in general it is not a descent method.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states liminf κ(d_k) = κ_* and then 'in particular' that κ(d_k) ↓ κ_*, i.e. monotone convergence of the whole objective sequence. A liminf statement does not imply convergence of the sequence, let alone monotone decrease, and the paper itself notes Algorithm GD is not a descent method; Kiwiel's Theorem 1 yields only liminf f(x_k)=f_* and monotone convergence of the best-so-far values f_*^k. The quantity κ_*^j is defined in the statement but never used, indicating the intended claim was κ_*^j ↓ κ_*.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'κ(D̊(d_k)) ↓ κ_*' by 'κ_*^j ↓ κ_*' (best-iterate convergence), which is what Kiwiel's Theorem 1 provides.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic guarantee for Algorithm GD as written (convergence of the full objective sequence) is unsupported; only best-iterate convergence liminf κ(d_k) = κ_* (equivalently κ_*^j ↓ κ_*) is established.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-1 asserts monotone convergence of the objective sequence, which the cited subgradient theory does not give and which contradicts the paper's own remark
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction to the statement, using an already-defined quantity, restores agreement with the proof; the algorithmic guarantee actually needed (best-iterate asymptotic convergence) is preserved and nothing depends on full-sequence monotonicity.
